Driver.title: Driver
Driver.description: Represents a driver employed by Transportes Especiales J&J. This entity supports the 'Conductores' module for managing driver information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Driver entity.

firstName.description: The first name of the driver.

lastName.description: The last name of the driver.

email.description: The email address of the driver.

phoneNumber.description: The contact phone number of the driver.

hireDate.description: The date when the driver was hired.

status.description: The current employment status of the driver (e.g., Active, Inactive, On Leave).

dateOfBirth.description: The date of birth of the driver.

address.description: The residential address of the driver.

Vehicle.title: Vehicle
Vehicle.description: Represents a vehicle in the fleet of Transportes Especiales J&J. This entity supports the 'Vehículos' module for tracking vehicle information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Vehicle entity.

licensePlate.description: The unique license plate number of the vehicle.

model.description: The specific model of the vehicle.

year.description: The manufacturing year of the vehicle.

capacity.description: The maximum passenger capacity of the vehicle.

acquisitionDate.description: The date when the vehicle was acquired by the company.

status.description: The current operational status of the vehicle (e.g., Available, In Service, Maintenance, Out of Service).

Client.title: Client
Client.description: Represents a client who uses the transportation services. This entity supports the 'Facturación y Cartera' module for billing purposes.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Client entity.

name.description: The name of the client (e.g., company name or individual name).

contactPerson.description: The name of the primary contact person for the client.

email.description: The email address of the client or contact person.

phoneNumber.description: The contact phone number of the client.

address.description: The physical address of the client.

Service.title: Service
Service.description: Represents a scheduled or completed transportation service provided by J&J Connect V2.0. This entity supports the 'Servicios' module.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Service entity.

description.description: A brief description or name of the service.

clientId.description: Reference to the Client requesting the service. (Relationship: Client 1:N Service)

driverId.description: Reference to the Driver assigned to this service. (Relationship: Driver 1:N Service)

vehicleId.description: Reference to the Vehicle used for this service. (Relationship: Vehicle 1:N Service)

startTime.description: The scheduled or actual start time of the service.

endTime.description: The scheduled or actual end time of the service.

startLocation.description: The starting location of the service.

endLocation.description: The destination location of the service.

status.description: The current status of the service (e.g., Scheduled, In Progress, Completed, Cancelled).

passengerCount.description: The number of passengers transported during the service.

estimatedCost.description: The estimated cost of the service.

actualCost.description: The actual cost incurred for the service. Used for profitability analysis.

distanceKm.description: The total distance covered by the service in kilometers.

Invoice.title: Invoice
Invoice.description: Represents an invoice issued to a client for transportation services. This entity supports the 'Facturación y Cartera' module.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Invoice entity.

invoiceNumber.description: The unique number assigned to the invoice.

clientId.description: Reference to the Client to whom the invoice is issued. (Relationship: Client 1:N Invoice)

serviceIds.description: References to the Services included in this invoice. (Relationship: Service N:N Invoice)

issueDate.description: The date when the invoice was issued.

dueDate.description: The date by which the invoice payment is due.

totalAmount.description: The total amount due for the invoice.

status.description: The current status of the invoice (e.g., Issued, Paid, Overdue, Cancelled).

paymentDate.description: The date when the invoice was paid (if applicable).

Payment.title: Payment
Payment.description: Represents a payment received from a client against an invoice. This entity supports the 'Facturación y Cartera' module.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Payment entity.

invoiceId.description: Reference to the Invoice this payment is for. (Relationship: Invoice 1:N Payment)

amount.description: The amount of money received in this payment.

paymentDate.description: The date when the payment was received.

paymentMethod.description: The method used for the payment (e.g., Bank Transfer, Cash, Credit Card).

transactionId.description: An optional external transaction identifier for the payment.

LocationUpdate.title: LocationUpdate
LocationUpdate.description: Represents a real-time location update for a vehicle. This entity supports the 'Monitoreo' module for tracking vehicle positions.

id.description: Unique identifier for the LocationUpdate entity.

vehicleId.description: Reference to the Vehicle whose location is being updated. (Relationship: Vehicle 1:N LocationUpdate)

serviceId.description: Optional reference to the Service currently being performed by the vehicle during this update. (Relationship: Service 1:N LocationUpdate)

timestamp.description: The exact date and time when the location update was recorded.

latitude.description: The latitude coordinate of the vehicle's location.

longitude.description: The longitude coordinate of the vehicle's location.

speedKmH.description: The speed of the vehicle at the time of the update in kilometers per hour.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore structure for J&J Connect V2.0 prioritizes security, scalability, and debuggability following the core design principles. Given the application's current scope of a single administrative user ('transportes.especialesjyj@gmail.com') managing all data, authorization is simplified but designed for future extensibility.

**Authorization Independence (CRITICAL):**
Authorization independence is achieved by storing all core business entities (`Driver`, `Vehicle`, `Client`, `Service`, `Invoice`, `LocationUpdate`) in top-level collections. This design ensures that security rules for these documents can be evaluated without needing to perform `get()` operations on parent documents. For instance, a `Service` document directly contains `clientId`, `driverId`, and `vehicleId` as foreign keys, meaning its access doesn't depend on fetching the associated `Client`, `Driver`, or `Vehicle` documents. This allows for atomic operations and simplifies rule logic considerably. 

For the `Payment` subcollection (`/invoices/{invoiceId}/payments/{paymentId}`), its authorization is intrinsically linked to the parent `Invoice`. In this admin-only context, a `get()` on the parent `Invoice` for authorization is not strictly necessary as access to both parent and child will be uniformly granted to the admin. If multi-client access were introduced, `clientId` (from the parent `Invoice`) would be denormalized into each `Payment` document to maintain authorization independence at the `Payment` level.

The global administrative role is managed via a dedicated `/admins/{adminId}` collection. Authorization for all data is determined by checking for the *existence* of `request.auth.uid` within this collection (`exists(/databases/$(database)/documents/admins/$(request.auth.uid))`). This is an atomic and highly efficient check, completely independent of the business data structure, fulfilling Authorization Independence at the highest level (DBAC).

**QAPs (Rules are not Filters):**
Secure `list` operations (Query-Appended Permissions) are inherently supported by the chosen structure and single-admin model. By segregating all data into top-level collections (e.g., `/drivers`, `/vehicles`, `/clients`, `/services`, `/invoices`, `/location_updates`), and granting broad read/write access to the authenticated admin, all queries performed by the admin will return results without being silently filtered by security rules. The admin has full visibility and control over all data. The `payments` subcollection similarly allows for secure listing of payments associated with a specific invoice.

**Structural Segregation & Access Modeling:**
All documents within a given collection (`/drivers`, `/vehicles`, etc.) share the same security posture (admin-only access), adhering to the Structural Segregation principle. This simplifies security rules, as there's no need to differentiate access based on document content within a collection (e.g., no mixing of 'public' vs 'private' records). Access modeling primarily uses Global Roles via the `/admins/{adminId}` collection. Hierarchical paths are used for logically nested data like `/invoices/{invoiceId}/payments/{paymentId}`, which naturally groups payments under their respective invoices.

**Data Clarity and Predictability:**
Consistent naming conventions are used for collections (plural entity names) and wildcards (e.g., `{driverId}`, `{vehicleId}`). Entities like `Driver`, `Vehicle`, `Service`, and `Invoice` use a dedicated `status` field for explicit state modeling, enhancing clarity and predictability of data state.
